alt: Alberta register a business name page with the Types of business names section and the trade name description highlighted
caption: Read Alberta's Types of business names. A trade name is what you register when you do business under a name other than your own personal name.

alt: Alberta register a business name page with the step about getting a Business Name Report from NUANS highlighted
caption: Before you register, consider a NUANS Business Name Report. Alberta recommends one to find similar names, but it is optional and NUANS members charge for it.

alt: Alberta register a business name page with the Declaration of Trade Name form link highlighted
caption: Fill in the Declaration of Trade Name form before you visit a registry agent. Partnerships use a different form.

alt: Alberta find a business registry page with the level 1 basic registrations list and the note that service fees vary highlighted
caption: Find a registry agent that handles basic registrations, which include trade names. Service fees are not regulated and vary between agents, so ask for the total before you go.

alt: City of Calgary open a retail business page with online or phone sales and home-based retail sales highlighted in the list of businesses that need a licence
caption: Each municipality sets its own rules. Calgary, for example, lists online or phone sales and home-based retail sales among the businesses that need a licence. Look up your own city or town in the same way.

alt: Name Request page with the action selector for starting a new business name
caption: Open Name Request and choose the action that matches what you're doing. For a new business, pick the option to get a business name.

alt: Name Request page with the How to Build Your Name guidance
caption: Read How to Build Your Name before you type anything. A name needs a distinctive part and a description, and it must not clash with an existing name.

alt: BC Registries and Online Services home page with the Create Account button highlighted
caption: Start at the BC Registries home page and choose Create Account.

alt: Create account page offering sign-in with BC Services Card
caption: Accounts are created with a BC Services Card. Have it set up before you start.

alt: Name Request page with the action selector
caption: Check and reserve your business name with Name Request before registering.

alt: eTaxBC log on page with the Enrol now option highlighted
caption: On the eTaxBC home page, use Enrol now to create an eTaxBC profile. You'll register for PST from inside your profile.

alt: CRA business registration page with the Register with Business Registration Online link highlighted
caption: On the CRA business registration page, choose Register with Business Registration Online (BRO).

alt: CRA page listing ways to register for a business number and program accounts
caption: This section explains what a business number covers and which program accounts (like GST/HST) you can add to it.

alt: CRA GST/HST for businesses page with the Who needs to register section highlighted
caption: Check Who needs to register for GST/HST. Most businesses must register once taxable sales pass $30,000 in four consecutive calendar quarters.

alt: CRA GST/HST for businesses page with the Get a GST/HST number and manage your account section highlighted
caption: When you're ready, open Get a GST/HST number and manage your account. Registration is done in Business Registration Online, signed in with your CRA account.

alt: Manitoba choose your business structure page with the sole proprietorship section and the personal liability point highlighted
caption: Read Manitoba's guide to business structures. A sole proprietorship is the simplest way to start, but the owner is personally liable for all business debts.

alt: Manitoba Companies Office business names page with the link to information on choosing a business name highlighted
caption: Read the Companies Office guidelines for choosing a business name before you request a name reservation.

alt: Manitoba Companies Office business name forms and fees page with the Request for Name Reservation row highlighted
caption: Start with a Request for Name Reservation. It costs $45, and an approved name is held for 90 days.

alt: Manitoba Companies Office business name forms and fees page with the Business Name Registration row highlighted
caption: Then file the Business Name Registration. Filing online is fastest, and it costs $60 for three years.

alt: Manitoba Finance taxation page with the Sign up for TAXcess link and the Do I Need to Register link highlighted
caption: Check Do I Need to Register?, then sign up for TAXcess and register for a retail sales tax account. Registration is free.

alt: City of Winnipeg home-based business page with the sentence saying a home-based business development permit is required highlighted
caption: Each municipality sets its own rules. Winnipeg, for example, needs a home-based business development permit if business mail comes to your home or you do the paperwork there. Look up your own municipality in the same way.

alt: Service New Brunswick Corporate Registry page with the Register a business name link highlighted
caption: Service New Brunswick's Corporate Registry registers the business names sole proprietors trade under. You only need it if you use a name other than your own.

alt: Service New Brunswick register or renew a business name page with the sentence on who must register highlighted
caption: Register your business name if you trade under any name other than your own. File within two months of starting.

alt: Service New Brunswick register or renew a business name page on the Fees tab with the Certificate of Business Name fee highlighted
caption: A Certificate of Business Name costs $112, including the $12 Royal Gazette fee. Renewing it every five years costs $62.

alt: City of Fredericton zoning and land use page with the question about having a home based business highlighted
caption: Each municipality sets its own rules. Fredericton, for example, allows a home occupation in a single detached house or mini-home, under its zoning by-law. Look up your own city or town in the same way.

alt: City of St. John's starting a business page with the link to its guide to municipal regulations for business highlighted
caption: Each municipality sets its own rules. St. John's, for example, publishes a guide to the municipal regulations and permits that apply to businesses. Look up your own city or town in the same way.

alt: Nova Scotia choose a legal structure page with the sole proprietorship description highlighted
caption: Read Nova Scotia's guide to legal structures. A sole proprietorship is a business owned by one person and not incorporated.

alt: Nova Scotia register a sole proprietorship page with the $68.55 registration fee highlighted
caption: Reserve your name first, then register the sole proprietorship. Registration costs $68.55 and must be renewed every year for the same fee.

alt: Halifax home improvement permits page on the Home Based Business tab with the development permit requirement highlighted
caption: Each municipality sets its own rules. Halifax, for example, needs a development permit for a home-based business. Look up your own municipality in the same way.

alt: NWT Corporate Registries business names page on the entity types tab with the proprietorship description highlighted
caption: A proprietorship is owned by one person, with no legal distinction between you and the business, so you are personally liable.

alt: NWT Corporate Registries business names forms tab with the sole proprietorship forms highlighted
caption: Download the sole proprietorship forms and mail or deliver the signed originals. Reservation is $25 and registration $50.

alt: City of Yellowknife business licences page with the home based business application highlighted
caption: Every business in the Northwest Territories needs a licence. In Yellowknife, a home-based business applies for a City licence and development permit together.

alt: Nunavut Legal Registries partnerships and business names page with the 60-day registration rule and the fee schedule link highlighted
caption: Register a business name with Nunavut Legal Registries within 60 days of first using it. The fee is $50.

alt: Ontario page on choosing an ownership structure with the sole proprietorship section highlighted
caption: Read Ontario's guide to ownership structures. A sole proprietorship is the simplest way to start, but you are personally liable for the business.

alt: Ontario Business Registry page with the search link highlighted
caption: Search the Ontario Business Registry to check that no one else is already using the name you want.

alt: Ontario register your business online page with the email and card requirement and the sole proprietorship fee highlighted
caption: Check what you need before you start: a working email address and a debit or credit card. You create an Ontario.ca Login and an Ontario Business Account during set-up, and a sole proprietorship costs $60.

alt: Ontario page listing registration fees with the sole proprietorship new registration fee highlighted
caption: Registering a sole proprietorship online costs $60 and takes effect immediately. Renewing it every five years costs the same $60.

alt: City of Toronto business regulations page with the list of businesses that do not need a licence open and the retail stores item highlighted
caption: Each city sets its own rules. Toronto, for example, says retail stores selling new, non-food items do not need a municipal operating licence. Look up your own city or town's licensing page in the same way.

alt: WordPress admin Products menu with Variation Converter and its Combine, Split and History tabs highlighted
caption: After you activate the plugin, open Products > Variation Converter. It has three tabs: Combine, Split and History.

alt: Variation Converter Combine tab filtered to the Ready view, with the Ready link and the Ready status of the listed groups highlighted
caption: Start with the Ready view. These groups have no warnings, so they are the quickest to combine. Work through Needs review after.

alt: Classic Crew Tee group opened for review, with the Black label and the Create variable product button highlighted
caption: Open a group to review it. Check the label for each product, untick any that don't belong, then click Create variable product.

alt: Variation Converter after creating the Classic Crew Tee variable product, with the success message highlighted
caption: The four tees are now one variable product with a Color option. The originals are hidden, not deleted, and Undo conversion puts them back.

alt: Classic Crew Tee product page in the shop with the Color menu highlighted
caption: In your shop, shoppers now see one Classic Crew Tee and pick a color from the menu.

alt: Variation Converter Split tab with the Canvas Apron variable product opened, its new product names and the Split button highlighted
caption: On the Split tab, open a variable product. Check the name each new product will get, untick any you don't want, then click Split.

alt: All Products list with the new Canvas Apron Sand and Canvas Apron Charcoal simple products highlighted
caption: Each variation is now its own simple product with its SKU, price and stock. The variable product stays in your list but is hidden from the shop.

alt: Variation Converter History tab listing a combine and a split, with an Undo button highlighted
caption: History lists every conversion, newest first. Undo puts the products back the way they were.

alt: Québec.ca legal forms of enterprise page with the sentence saying a sole proprietorship has no legal existence separate from its owner highlighted
caption: Read Quebec's guide to legal forms. A sole proprietorship has no legal existence separate from you, so you are personally liable for its debts.

alt: Québec.ca about registration page with the rule on sole proprietorships that must register highlighted
caption: Register with the Registraire des entreprises if your business name doesn't include your first and last names. Registration costs $41.

alt: Montréal get an occupancy permit page for Le Plateau-Mont-Royal with the sentence about using part of your home for professional purposes highlighted
caption: Each municipality sets its own rules. In Montréal, a certificate of occupancy is needed to use part of your home for professional purposes, and fees vary by borough. Check with your own municipality or borough.

alt: Saskatchewan Corporate Registry choose a business type page with the sole proprietorship option highlighted
caption: Read the Corporate Registry's guide to business types. A sole proprietorship is the simplest way to start.

alt: Saskatchewan Corporate Registry search and reserve a business name page with the name reservation expiry rule highlighted
caption: Reserve your business name before you register it. A reservation costs $50 and is held for 90 days.

alt: Government of Saskatchewan apply for a PST number page with the online new business registration through SETS highlighted
caption: Register for a PST vendor's licence online through Saskatchewan eTax Services (SETS).

alt: City of Saskatoon home-based business licence page with the $135 new licence fee highlighted
caption: Each municipality sets its own rules. Saskatoon, for example, charges $135 for a new home-based business licence and $95 a year to renew. Look up your own city or town in the same way.

alt: City of Whitehorse business licence page with the business licence information highlighted
caption: Each community sets its own rules. Whitehorse, for example, licenses every business and needs a development permit for a home business. Look up your own community in the same way.
